headline: Large Energy User Grid Cost Shifting
short_summary: This bill directs Dominion Energy to propose tariffs that shift certain capacity and distribution infrastructure costs to large energy users, primarily data centers, rather than residential customers.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Residential consumer advocates, Dominion Energy, Senator Louise Lucas, Senator Mark Warner.
opponents: Data center industry (Data Center Coalition), large industrial users.
news_headline: Virginia Governor Signs Dominion-Backed Bills, All Eyes on Regulators Now
news_summary: Governor Spanberger signed legislation directing regulators to assign electricity costs to data centers, removing a prior requirement for data centers to cover capacity market costs but giving the SCC broader authority to protect residential customers from these costs. The bill aims to prevent residential customers from bearing electricity generation and distribution costs for data centers, which have contributed to rising bills.

headline: Data Center Water Use Reporting
short_summary: This bill requires water suppliers to report the total volume of potable and reclaimed water provided to data centers, increasing transparency on their water consumption.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups, local governments, water conservation advocates, Senator Kannan Srinivasan, Delegate Elizabeth Guzman, Delegate Shelly Simonds.
opponents: Data center industry (due to reporting burden/potential scrutiny).
news_headline: New Virginia law requires data center water usage be made public
news_summary: A new state law, SB 553, mandates local water authorities to report data center water usage, making the numbers publicly available on the Department of Environmental Quality's website starting January 1, 2027. This legislation, championed by Senator Kannan Srinivasan, aims to provide transparency regarding the water consumption of the rapidly growing data center industry in Virginia.

headline: Data Center Siting and Noise
short_summary: This bill requires site assessments for noise impacts on nearby residential units and schools for new high energy use facilities and allows localities to require assessments of other environmental impacts.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local residents, community groups, environmental advocates (e.g., Virginia League of Conservation Voters, Piedmont Environmental Council), Delegate Joshua E. Thomas, Delegate Elizabeth R. Guzman, Delegate Dan I. Helmer, Delegate John Chilton McAuliff, Delegate David A. Reid.
opponents: Data center developers, real estate industry (Data Center Coalition).
news_headline: Loudoun County Pauses New Data Center Applications for a Year
news_summary: Loudoun County, a major data center hub, has approved a one-year pause on processing new data center applications to update siting standards and address compatibility issues. This pause will allow the county to consider restrictions on siting near residential areas, height limits, and noise levels, reflecting growing community concerns.
